Several other chemical classes, including ureido sulfonamides and glycosyl coumarins, have consequently been investigated as selective CA IX/XII inhibitors.

According to the retracted study, MMP-2 downregulation decreased TNF-α, TNFR1, TRADD, TRAF2, and RIP expression and disrupted interactions between TRADD and TRAF2, thereby attenuating TNF-α-induced NF-κB activation. Because NF-κB commonly promotes expression of survival-associated genes, this loss of signaling was proposed to make glioma cells more susceptible to programmed cell death.

Summary: Vitamin D Receptor Polymorphisms and Gestational Hypertension

The case-control study “Role of Vitamin-D Receptor (VDR) single nucleotide polymorphisms in gestational hypertension development” investigated whether maternal vitamin D status and VDR genetic variants, particularly FokI and BsmI polymorphisms and their haplotypes, were associated with susceptibility to gestational hypertension.

The study reported that vitamin D deficiency was associated with approximately a threefold higher risk of gestational hypertension, whereas normal vitamin D status appeared protective. Hypovitaminosis D was common among both groups, but deficiency was more frequent among women with gestational hypertension. The authors also reported that the VDR FF/bB haplotype was associated with roughly twice the risk of gestational hypertension compared with other haplotypes.

Importantly, the findings suggested an interaction between genetic background and vitamin D status. Adequate vitamin D levels appeared to attenuate the increased risk associated with unfavorable VDR FokI/BsmI haplotypes, while vitamin D deficiency appeared to amplify it. On this basis, the authors proposed that VDR genotyping combined with vitamin D assessment might eventually support individualized vitamin D supplementation strategies during pregnancy.

Critical reliability note

This study has been retracted, as indicated in the supplied metadata. Consequently, its reported associations, effect sizes, gene-vitamin D interactions, and proposed clinical implications should not be treated as reliable evidence or used to guide screening, VDR genotyping, vitamin D supplementation, or management of gestational hypertension.

Other case-control evidence in the supplied context reports an association between low vitamin D levels and gestational hypertension/preeclampsia, including lower mean vitamin D concentrations among affected women and an estimated odds ratio of 2.76 for vitamin D deficiency. However, these observations do not independently validate the retracted study's specific VDR polymorphism or haplotype findings, and observational associations do not by themselves establish causality.

Bottom line: The retracted study proposed that vitamin D deficiency and particular VDR FokI/BsmI haplotypes jointly influence gestational hypertension susceptibility, but these specific conclusions should now be regarded as unsupported by that publication and requiring confirmation from independent, non-retracted research.
